body: Wind with one clear direction and strength: hair and loose clothes (abaya, scarf, shemagh ends) stream that way, palm fronds bend and rattle, flags snap, dust and plastic bags skitter along the ground, people squint and lean slightly into it, hold their scarf; gusts come in waves, not constant. Sound: whooshing, rustling leaves, flapping fabric.

Iraqi dust storm (عجاج): the sky turns orange-brown, the sun is a pale disc, visibility drops to a few hundred metres, buildings fade into haze, fine dust swirls at street level, people cover nose and mouth with scarves or shemagh, cars drive with headlights on; everything has a warm sepia tint and soft shadows.

Real rain: streaks visible against dark backgrounds and lights, splashes and rings on puddles, wet surfaces mirror lights and turn darker, water runs off roofs and gutters, clothes darken where wet and stick, hair clumps, people hurry with umbrellas or newspapers over their heads, car tyres hiss; sound of drops on different surfaces (metal roof, glass, pavement) plus distant thunder for storms.

Real water: surface reflects the sky and surroundings with ripples breaking the reflection, small waves move in one direction, sunlight glitters on it, the colour shifts with depth (Tigris and Euphrates are muddy green-brown, the Gulf at Basra is grey-green), splashes form crowns and droplets that fall back with gravity, wet skin glistens; sound of lapping, flowing or crashing water.

Splash physics: on entry the water forms a crater and a crown of droplets, then a column, spray falls back in arcs, ripples spread in rings and bounce off edges, bubbles trail underwater; a swimmer's hair flattens and drips when they come up, they wipe their face and blow out a breath.

Real fire: flames flicker and lick upward with yellow-orange tips and a blue base, embers glow and float up, heat shimmer distorts the air above, warm flickering light dances on nearby faces and walls, smoke rises and drifts with the wind; charcoal grills (منقل) glow red with fat dripping and flaring; sound of crackling and sizzling.

Smoke and steam: steam rises from hot tea, food and kettles in soft curling wisps that fade within a short distance; smoke is denser, catches light in beams, drifts with the air and thins out; fog softens distant objects and makes light sources glow.

Doors done right: the hand reaches for the real handle, turns it, the door swings on its hinges at believable speed with its own weight, light from the other side spills in as it opens, the person steps through and turns to close it; sound of the latch click, hinge creak for old doors, a soft thud or slam matching the force.

Impacts and breaking (non-graphic, nobody hurt): the moving object decelerates on contact and both objects react with weight (dents, bounce, slide), glass cracks in radiating lines then shatters into sharp pieces that fall with gravity and scatter, dust or debris puffs out; the sound arrives exactly on contact – crunch, crack, tinkling glass – followed by settling pieces. Keep any car accident minor with people safe.

A real jump: the person crouches first (knees bend, arms swing back), pushes off with both feet, arms swing up, the body rises and slows at the top, clothes and hair lift slightly with the motion, then falls and lands toe-to-heel with knees bending to absorb the impact, a slight wobble and a breath; feet never float or slide.

Real running: arms swing opposite to the legs, the body leans forward slightly, the foot strikes under the body and pushes off, there is a short moment with both feet off the ground, clothes and hair bounce with each stride, breathing becomes audible and rhythmic, footsteps match the surface (slap on tile, crunch on gravel, thud on dirt).

A real walk: heel strikes first then rolls to the toe, opposite arm swings, the hips and shoulders counter-rotate slightly, the head bobs gently, each person has their own rhythm (hurried, relaxed, swaying); feet stay planted on the ground with no sliding, and footsteps are heard in sync.

Things that fall accelerate (slow at first, then fast), tumble according to their shape (paper flutters, a phone flips, a ball bounces lower each time), and react on impact (a cup cracks, liquid splashes outward); a person who slips catches themselves with arms out and recovers with a laugh – nobody gets hurt.

Throwing and catching: the thrower winds up with the whole body, the object follows a clean arc (parabola) with gravity, spins if it should, the catcher's eyes track it, hands open before it arrives and close around it with a small give backward on impact.

Fabric physics: light fabrics (chiffon, silk, cotton dishdasha) flow and lag behind movement and settle softly; heavy fabrics (wool, denim, velvet curtains) swing slower with fewer folds; fabric creases at elbows, waist and knees, stretches over the shoulders when arms lift, and reacts to wind in the scene's direction.

Pouring liquid: a smooth stream that narrows as it falls, splashes slightly where it lands, the level rises in the glass with a small swirl, bubbles or foam for soda and coffee crema, a drop runs down the outside of the spout; tea poured from a height arcs and makes a light bubbling sound.

Sunlight by time: sunrise is soft pink-gold with long cool shadows; Iraqi midday is harsh white light from overhead with short dark shadows, heat haze over asphalt and people squinting; golden hour is warm orange from a low side angle with long shadows and glowing edges on hair; after sunset the sky goes orange-to-violet and streetlights start glowing.

Night realism: mixed light sources with different colours (warm sodium streetlights, cool white LED shop signs, colourful neon, car headlights and red tail-lights), deep shadows with some noise, bright lights bloom slightly, faces lit from one side by a shop window or phone screen, the sky dark blue not pure black, and a quieter ambience with distant traffic and dogs.

Iraqi summer heat (45°C+): blinding white light, heat haze shimmering above roads, people seek shade under awnings and trees, sweat on foreheads and dark patches on shirts, fanning with a hand or paper, cold water bottles with condensation, AC units dripping on walls, empty streets at noon.

Cold weather: visible breath clouds, people in coats and scarves with hands in pockets, red noses and cheeks, shivering shoulders, snow (in the Kurdistan mountains) falling in slow flakes and settling on hair and shoulders, footprints in snow with a crunch sound.

Reflections must be correct: a mirror shows the reversed scene from the right angle and moves exactly with the person, shop windows show faint reflections of the street over what is inside, shiny cars reflect the sky and buildings, and the reflection never shows anything that is not in the scene.

Shadows follow the light: every person and object casts one in the same direction from the main light, sharp in direct sun and soft in shade or cloud, contact shadows where feet and objects touch the ground, and shadows move with the body.

Vehicles in motion: wheels turn at the speed the car moves (no spinning-in-place), the body leans slightly in turns and dips when braking, dust kicks up behind on dirt roads, reflections slide across the paint, the driver's hands turn the wheel and the head checks mirrors; engine sound rises with acceleration, tyres hum, indicators tick.
Paper and books: pages bend and turn with a curl, catch light, flutter in wind, have readable texture and slight transparency; a book opens with its spine flexing, a page turn makes a soft rustle.

Eating and drinking for real: the hand brings food to the mouth (Iraqis often eat with bread or the right hand), the mouth opens just enough, chewing moves jaw and cheeks, a happy 'mmm' reaction with closed eyes or a nod, the throat moves when swallowing; drinks: lips meet the rim, the glass tilts, the level drops, a satisfied exhale after a cold drink.

Phones and screens: thumbs tap the screen in the right places, the screen glow lights the face, the screen content is plausible (chat app, video, map) and readable when it matters, the person reacts to what they see (smile, surprise); laptop typing shows fingers on the keys with a soft clatter.

Machines work like real machines: moving parts move for a reason (belts turn wheels, pistons push, fans spin at a steady speed), lights and screens respond to button presses, vibration and small rattles are visible, and the sound matches (hum, whir, clicks, beeps) in sync with what happens.
